title: CHIEF OF THE NAVAL STAFF ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO MAURITIUS TO STRENGTHEN BILATERAL MARITIME COOPERATION
body_text:
Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), is on a four-day official visit to Mauritius from 10 to 13 Aug 2026. The visit is part of India's continued engagement to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation and deepen defence ties with Mauritius, an extremely valued partner in the Indian Ocean Region.
During the visit, the CNS will interact with senior leadership of the Government of Mauritius and hold discussions on matters of mutual interest such as maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration.
Such engagements are aimed at strengthening Indo-Mauritius cooperation in the maritime domain, enhancing operational-level linkages and consolidating the robust strategic partnership between India and Mauritius .
India and Mauritius share a close and enduring maritime partnership . The Indian Navy engages regularly with the National Coast Guard through training exchanges, operational interactions including Joint Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) Surveillance, port visits and hydrographic surveys. Both countries also participate and engage with each other in multilateral forums and cooperative initiatives. Mauritius has been a regular participant in key Indian Navy initiatives such as the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, MILAN, International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME, aptly reflecting the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) they share.
The visit of Admiral Krishna Swaminathan to Mauritius after assuming charge as the Chief of the Naval Staff underscores the priority India accords to the friendship it shares with Mauritius, anchored in mutual respect, trust and a shared commitment to maritime security, regional cooperation and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.
***
VM/AS

enrichment.summary: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, is on a four-day official visit to Mauritius from 10 to 13 August 2026 to strengthen bilateral maritime cooperation. He will engage with senior Mauritian leadership on maritime security, defence cooperation, capacity building and military collaboration. The visit builds on existing India-Mauritius naval engagement including joint EEZ surveillance, training exchanges, port visits and hydrographic surveys, and reflects India's MAHASAGAR vision for the Indian Ocean Region.
enrichment.context:
Mauritius occupies a strategically important position in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and has long been considered one of India's closest maritime partners, given historical, cultural and diaspora linkages as well as its location astride key sea lanes. India has provided Mauritius with naval vessels, offshore patrol ships, coastal surveillance radar systems, and helicopters, and Indian Navy/Coast Guard personnel are deployed to support Mauritius's National Coast Guard. This cooperation forms part of India's broader 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) doctrine, now evolving into the MAHASAGAR framework, which emphasizes mutual and holistic advancement of security and economic growth across the Indian Ocean littoral and beyond.

Such high-level visits by the Chief of the Naval Staff soon after assuming office are customary diplomatic-cum-strategic gestures signaling continuity and priority in bilateral defence relationships. Mauritius's regular participation in India-led multilateral naval initiatives—such as MILAN, the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium (IONS), International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR, and Exercise AIKEYME—illustrates India's effort to build a cooperative maritime security architecture in the IOR, partly as a counterbalance to increasing Chinese naval and economic presence in the region, including in island states like Mauritius, Seychelles, Sri Lanka and Maldives.

prelims_questions.question: The 'MAHASAGAR' vision mentioned in the context of India's maritime engagement with Indian Ocean Region countries stands for:
options: Maritime and Holistic Approach for Strategic Alliance and Global Advancement in the Region
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
Multilateral Agreement for Harmonious Security and Governance Across Regions
Maritime Alliance for Humanitarian Assistance and Strategic Growth in Asia
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, MAHASAGAR stands for 'Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions', an evolution of India's earlier SAGAR doctrine for the Indian Ocean Region.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following is a multilateral naval initiative in which Mauritius regularly participates along with India, as mentioned in the release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifically names MILAN, along with the Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, International Fleet Review, Goa Maritime Conclave, IOS SAGAR and Exercise AIKEYME, as forums where Mauritius regularly engages with India.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of India's maritime cooperation with Indian Ocean island states like Mauritius in the context of India's SAGAR/MAHASAGAR vision. How does such cooperation contribute to regional maritime security architecture?
Examine the strategic importance of the Indian Ocean Region for India's national security, and analyze the role of naval diplomacy in strengthening India's ties with smaller littoral states.
